name: Inter-Frame Feature Consistency
description: Matches features across consecutive frames to detect temporal inconsistencies and object morphing in AI-generated video.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated or manipulated video by analyzing the consistency of visual features across consecutive frames — a fundamental property of authentic camera-captured video:

1. **Local Feature Extraction and Matching**: The method extracts robust local features (SuperPoint or ORB keypoints with descriptors) from each frame and matches them across consecutive frame pairs using nearest-neighbor matching with ratio test (Lowe's ratio = 0.7). In authentic video, matched features should satisfy geometric consistency — the matched point positions should be explainable by a single homography or fundamental matrix (epipolar geometry) corresponding to camera motion. The method computes the homography using RANSAC and measures the inlier ratio. Authentic video produces inlier ratios > 0.7 for rigid scenes. AI-generated video often produces lower inlier ratios because objects may morph or deform inconsistently between frames.

2. **Object Identity Persistence Tracking**: The method tracks individual objects across frames using appearance features (deep embedding from Re-ID networks) and validates that object identity remains consistent. In authentic video, an object's deep embedding should change gradually — the cosine similarity between embeddings of the same object across 10 frames should exceed 0.8. AI-generated video (especially from autoregressive or frame-by-frame generators) may produce objects that change identity — subtle appearance shifts in texture, color, or shape that accumulate over time, causing the embedding similarity to drop below 0.6 within 30 frames. This identity drift is imperceptible to casual viewers but detectable through embedding analysis.

3. **Texture Temporal Stability Analysis**: Static surfaces in authentic video maintain consistent texture across frames — the texture pattern of a wall, floor, or clothing remains the same (only changing due to camera motion, which is compensable). The method selects texture patches on static surfaces and measures their SSIM and phase correlation across frames after motion compensation. Authentic patches maintain SSIM > 0.9 across 30 frames. AI-generated video shows texture regeneration — static surfaces exhibit subtle texture changes between frames because the generator independently synthesizes texture per frame rather than maintaining a persistent 3D scene texture.

4. **Geometric Structure Temporal Consistency**: Rigid objects in authentic video maintain constant geometric properties — straight lines remain straight, parallel lines remain parallel, and angles between edges remain constant (changing only due to perspective projection, which follows well-defined geometric rules). The method detects line segments (LSD algorithm) and tracks geometric relationships across frames. In authentic video, vanishing points are temporally stable (they move smoothly with camera rotation). AI-generated video may produce inconsistent geometric structure — vanishing points that jump between frames, parallel lines that become non-parallel, or straight edges that develop curves — because the generator does not maintain an explicit 3D scene model.
parameters:
Feature extraction: SuperPoint (256-D descriptors)
Feature matching: nearest-neighbor with Lowe's ratio 0.7
Geometric verification: RANSAC homography, inlier ratio threshold > 0.7
Object tracking: Re-ID embeddings (cosine similarity)
Identity persistence threshold: cosine similarity > 0.8 over 10 frames
Texture stability: SSIM > 0.9 after motion compensation
Line detection: LSD (Line Segment Detector)
Vanishing point tracking: J-linkage clustering
Minimum video length: 15 frames
Analysis frame rate: every frame for features, every 5th for deep embeddings
accuracy: 84–92% accuracy detecting AI-generated video via inter-frame consistency. Feature correspondence inlier ratios achieve AUC of 0.89. Object identity persistence provides F1-score of 0.86 for autoregressive video generators. Texture temporal stability achieves AUC of 0.88. Geometric consistency provides the strongest signal for AI video with camera motion (AUC 0.91). Performance degrades for static-camera AI video with minimal scene complexity.
source: Gu, Z. et al. (2022). Delving into the Local: Dynamic Inconsistency Learning for DeepFake Video Detection. Proceedings of AAAI, 744–752.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated video content through temporal consistency analysis. Identifying video manipulation and frame splicing. Forensic authentication of surveillance and evidence footage. Quality assessment of video generation models for temporal coherence.
strengths:
• Comprehensive temporal consistency analysis across multiple signal types
• Feature correspondence exploits fundamental geometric constraints
• Object identity tracking detects gradual drift invisible to human viewers
• Texture stability analysis targets generator-specific frame-independence
• Geometric consistency is physics-based and interpretable
limitations:
• Static scenes with no texture provide limited feature matching signal
• Heavy video compression reduces feature quality and matching accuracy
• Very short clips (< 1 second) provide insufficient temporal data
• Advanced video generators with explicit temporal modeling produce more consistent output
• Natural scene changes (cuts, zooms) interrupt consistency analysis
